gates.description: Evaluation framework must be defined before LLM integration goes to production — no deployment without evals
PII must be detected and redacted before sending to external LLM APIs — no customer data leakage
Prompt injection attack vectors must be documented and mitigated for all user-facing LLM inputs
Token budget limits and cost alerts must be configured — no unbounded LLM spend
Hallucination risk assessed and mitigation defined — grounding, citations, or confidence thresholds required
Graceful degradation must be defined when LLM service is unavailable or returns errors

anti_patterns.description: Writing a prompt, shipping it to production, and hoping it works — no evaluation, no monitoring, no fallback
Reaching for fine-tuning before exhausting prompt engineering and RAG — fine-tuning is expensive and inflexible
Building a RAG pipeline without evaluating retrieval quality — garbage in, garbage out at scale
Stuffing the context window with everything available — costs explode as usage grows
Shipping an LLM feature for factual queries without citation or grounding — one bad answer becomes a support crisis
Sending user data to external LLM APIs without PII redaction — regulatory and reputational risk

escalation_triggers: LLM producing harmful, biased, or confidential content in production
Token costs growing faster than revenue — unit economics broken
Hallucination rate unacceptable and grounding strategies exhausted
LLM provider API reliability below SLA requirements
Prompt injection attack exploited in production
Evaluation shows model regression after provider model update

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with LLM use case requirements, safety constraints, and latency SLAs

output_certifications: Evaluation framework defined and passing before production deployment
PII detection and redaction implemented for all LLM API calls
Prompt injection vectors documented and mitigated
Token budget limits and cost alerts configured
Hallucination mitigation strategy defined (grounding, citations, or confidence threshold)
Graceful fallback behavior defined for LLM service unavailability
